subject: health
title: Correction and reflection: reporting pathways and what happens after a report
focus: reporting pathways and what happens after a report
essentialQuestion: How do I keep a disagreement from becoming a danger?
keyPoints: Reporting pathways may include school, workplace, platform, advocacy, or emergency channels; a useful report states observable facts, timing, location, and the requested safety response.
Use observable facts, reliable information, and the appropriate support route; do not infer a person’s health, motives, or character from one detail.

For reporting pathways and what happens after a report, a strong response distinguishes fact from assumption, uses a fictional or public case, and includes a safe next step or appropriate source of support.
privacySafeScenario: Take one fictional conflict from first friction to three different endings — repaired, disengaged, and reported — and justify which ending fits which conditions.
studentTask: Apply the lesson facts to a supplied fictional case about reporting pathways and what happens after a report. Produce a three-part response that identifies the key concept, chooses a safe and feasible action, and explains the choice with two details from the instruction plus an appropriate support route.
knowledgeCheck: In two or three sentences, explain the most important distinction in reporting pathways and what happens after a report; use one lesson fact and name the evidence, safety check, or support route that makes the explanation dependable.
completionCriteria: The response completes every named part of the reporting pathways and what happens after a report task using the supplied fictional or public case.
The response uses at least two accurate details from the lesson instruction and distinguishes evidence from assumption.
The response gives a safe, feasible next step or support route and does not depend on private disclosure, body comparison, or recorded media proof.
adaptationChoices: Branching may be diagrammed, written, narrated, or completed on a supplied decision-tree template. Verbal rehearsal is optional and never public.
extensionChallenge: Apply reporting pathways and what happens after a report under a new constraint, compare two approaches, or explain the idea to someone else with an original fictional example, without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
